settings.headline: Given back to the valley,
settings.subtitle: A private foundation started in 1993 by Eleanor and James Alder, with a board and staff who live in the region we serve.

settings.headline: From timber to
settings.body:
The Alder family logged these hills for three generations. In 1993, Eleanor and James Alder sold the company and put most of the proceeds into a foundation, with one instruction: spend it here, and let the people of the valley lead.

Today the endowment is about $212 million. We grant around 5 percent of it every year, and we have never funded outside the Alder River region.

Our board includes a tenant organizer, a tribal fisheries manager, a school librarian and a union electrician, alongside two Alder grandchildren. Half of our board seats are held by people who have led a grantee organization.

settings.headline: Three promises we make to
settings.body: We wrote these with our grantee advisory council in 2023, and we report on them every year.

values.title: An answer in three weeks
values.text: Every letter of inquiry gets a reply within three weeks, and every no comes with a reason.

values.title: No new paperwork
values.text: Send us the proposal and reports you already wrote for another funder.

values.title: A real conversation
values.text: Each program officer holds open office hours twice a month.
